item.title: New recombinant mpox strain detected in UK and India, WHO urges continued monitoring
item.description: The detection of a newly identified recombinant mpox virus containing genetic material from two known strains underscores the need for continued genomic surveillance, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) said on Saturday, as the overall global public health risk assessment remains unchanged.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Guterres tells AU Summit: ‘This is 2026 – not 1946’ in push for reform
item.description: Calling for sweeping reforms of global institutions, UN Secretary-General António Guterres told African leaders on Saturday that the absence of permanent African seats on the Security Council is “indefensible,” declaring: “This is 2026 – not 1946.”
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World Entrepreneurs and Investment Forum puts women at the heart of economic transformation
item.description: Women entrepreneurs must be recognized as the architects of economic change and not the beneficiaries.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: In the hands of innovators from the Global South, AI can transform lives
item.description: Artificial intelligence is no longer the sole preserve of rich western nations. The applications for the Global South, in areas ranging from health to agriculture and industry, are having a transformative effect on people’s lives.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: Deadly strikes in Sudan, health systems in South Sudan near the brink, Guterres calls for unity ahead of Ramadan.
item.description: A sharp increase in drone attacks across the Kordofan region in the centre of Sudan is endangering civilians and damaging critical infrastructure.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Gaza: Lifesaving aid operations continue despite restrictions
item.description: Humanitarians in the Gaza Strip continue to face impediments in their efforts to deliver lifesaving aid to the population.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Syria transition gains ground with Kurdish deal, but violence and humanitarian strain persist
item.description: Syria’s fragile political transition has gained fresh momentum with a landmark agreement between Damascus and Kurdish authorities in the northeast, but renewed violence in the south, Israeli incursions and deep humanitarian needs underscore how precarious the path to stability remains, senior UN officials told the Security Council on Friday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Like a scene out of a horror movie’: UN report warns of war crimes in Sudan’s El Fasher
item.description: Paramilitary forces in Sudan unleashed “a wave of intense violence…shocking in its scale and brutality” during their final offensive to capture the besieged city of El Fasher last October, committing atrocities that amount to war crimes and possible crimes against humanity, according to a report released on Friday by the UN human rights office, OHCHR.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Madagascar: ‘Overwhelming’ destruction, surging needs after back-to-back cyclones – WFP
item.description: Some 10 days after Tropical Cyclone Fytia brought heavy rains and flooding to Madagascar, Cyclone Gezani has left the island’s main port in ruins, the UN World Food Programme (WFP) said on Friday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Political violence against MPs rising worldwide
item.description: A majority of parliamentarians worldwide are facing threats and abuse from voters, according to a new report released by the Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU), which found that 71 per cent of lawmakers surveyed experienced violence from the public – whether offline, online or both.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN envoy urges renewed political push as Yemen tensions rise
item.description: The UN Special Envoy for Yemen on Thursday welcomed recent steps to bolster stability and improve living conditions, but told the Security Council that only a renewed political process can end the country’s long-running conflict.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: Türk slams relentless Russian attacks, Gaza update, Cyclone Gezani hits Madagascar
item.description: Amid reported heavy Russian strikes across Ukraine on Thursday, UN human rights chief Volker Türk has condemned the “continual bombardment” the country’s people are facing.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Protecting children in war is key to lasting peace, top UN envoy warns
item.description: After three decades of its mandate to protect children caught up in war, the UN’s top advocate on the issue is determined to remind the world that prevention and protection go hand in hand.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: From war zones to outer space, radio remains essential
item.description: Even as the world fixates on ever‑brighter screens and sprawling digital feeds, radio endures with a quiet resilience, shaping how we share experience and understand one another. Its waves travel where sight cannot, pairing with cutting‑edge innovation in some places and acting as a lone, indispensable lifeline in others when technology fails to keep pace.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Gaza radio station re-opens, bringing voices from the rubble
item.description: Broadcaster Rami Al-Sharafi works on a laptop inside the damaged Zaman FM radio station building in Gaza, marking what may seem an unlikely return to the airwaves amid the rubble of the deadly two-year Israel-Hamas war.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: World News in Brief: School shooting in Canada, cholera outbreak in DR Congo, evacuations in Gaza
item.description: The UN Secretary-General has expressed his sorrow over Tuesday’s deadly shooting at a school in rural Canada that left at least eight dead and 25 wounded.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Civilians and aid operations under fire as Sudan airstrikes intensify
item.description: Escalating aerial attacks in Sudan are killing children, damaging schools and striking United Nations facilities, placing civilians and humanitarian workers at growing risk, the UN warned on Wednesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Ukraine: UN aid convoy reaches frontlines in Dnipro
item.description: A UN humanitarian convoy reached frontline communities in Ukraine’s Dnipro region on Wednesday, delivering critical medical and hygiene supplies as fighting continues to take a heavy toll on civilians and infrastructure across the country.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: West Bank: UN rights chief warns against deepening Israeli control over Palestinian land
item.description: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk called on Wednesday for Israel to rescind recent measures to expand control over Palestinian lands in the occupied West Bank.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Measles cases drop in 2025 across Europe and Central Asia, but outbreak risks remain
item.description: Measles cases across Europe and Central Asia declined by 75 per cent in 2025 compared to 2024, according to preliminary data released on Wednesday by the World Health Organization (WHO), which warned of remaining outbreak risks.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN social policy commission closes with calls to turn pledges into action
item.description: With inequality deepening and trust in public institutions under strain, the UN’s main forum on social policy wrapped up its annual session on Tuesday with a renewed push to turn global commitments on social justice into action.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Women and girls in science: Dismantling barriers, closing gender gaps
item.description: Although women are more likely than young men to pursue higher education, they make up only 35 per cent of science graduates.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN warns civilians remain at risk as airstrikes continue across Gaza
item.description: Fresh airstrikes and shelling across the Gaza Strip over the past 24 hours have put civilians at renewed risk and compounded months of hardship, the UN said on Tuesday, warning that humanitarian needs continue to outpace access and capacity.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: In Bahrain; work, dignity and the quiet rise of home-grown enterprise
item.description: From a crochet hook in a Cairo living room to digital marketplaces reaching across borders, women entrepreneurs are demonstrating how creativity, persistence and targeted support can translate into livelihoods — even when formal employment is out of reach.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Violence surges in South Sudan leaving civilians at risk and peacekeepers stretched thin
item.description: Escalating violence, political stalemate and humanitarian constraints are pushing South Sudan’s civilians to the brink once again, while funding cuts weaken the UN mission tasked with protecting them.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: General Assembly President urges Europeans to ‘stand up’ for the UN
item.description: The President of the United Nations General Assembly appealed on Tuesday for Europe to protect the international rules-based system, defend the truth in the face of fake news and other falsehoods, and support UN reform.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Fresh report warns fish fraud extends to one fifth of global catch
item.description: Fish fraud is widespread in markets, grocers and restaurants around the world, but a growing number of innovative tools are turning the tide, according to a new report published on Tuesday by the UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO).
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: In Sudan, sick and starving children ‘wasting away’
item.description: Relentless violence, famine and disease are fuelling a rising death toll among children in Sudan, while attacks on healthcare and a lack of aid access hamper efforts to help them, UN aid agencies warned on Tuesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Ethiopia: Türk fears new crisis in Tigray amid renewed fighting
item.description: UN human rights chief Volker Türk appealed on Tuesday to all parties involved in renewed heavy fighting in Ethiopia’s ‘precarious’ Tigray region to step back, warning of the potential for a deepening crisis in the country’s war-weary north and beyond.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Proposed amnesty law offers political prisoners in Venezuela an ‘opportunity’
item.description: A draft amnesty law in Venezuela aimed at granting immediate clemency to people jailed for participating in political protests or criticizing public figures, has been welcomed by a UN commission of experts – although they have emphasised the Venezuelan people need to be at the centre of the process.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories
